module: Editor "Traffic Manager": lets you compose a traffic session (vehicles and props placed on the map, traffic lights, signs), start/stop the simulation (AI of unlocked vehicles, signals), then save the session as JSON with an associated prefab. Windows: main (trafficEditMode edit mode), "Traffic Vehicles & Props", "Traffic Lights", "Traffic Signs" and "Options". Created objects are stored in the "TrafficSession" SimGroup. A modder uses it through the editor menu; the public Lua API is limited to loading/saving a session, reading the data and the simulation.
notes: The session file contains: name, author, description, level, version (1), includePlayerVehicle, signalsKeepOriginal, signalsSaveApart, debugMode, vehicles, signals {instances, controllers, sequences}.
loadSession and saveSession replace .prefab.json with .json in the path (unescaped pattern: the dot is a wildcard) to work on the data file; a prefab of the same name is generated/loaded alongside.
If the file's level differs from the current level and M.assertLevel is true, a confirmation is requested; accepting disables assertLevel until it is re-enabled.
saveSession refuses to write (notification "Missing session data!") if there is no vehicle, no light and no sign.
On save, each vehicle is teleported in place (spawn.safeTeleport) and the fields aiActive, stats and _tempData are not written.
onSerialize returns an empty table and onDeserialize does nothing: the session is not kept across a Lua reload.

assertLevel.desc: True by default: loadSession compares the file's level with the current level and asks for confirmation if they differ.

debugMode.desc: False by default: enables debug drawing (AI target, box under the vehicle) even for active vehicles; copied from the loaded file.

enableSimulation.desc: Starts the simulation: enables the AI of all unlocked vehicles and the signals, reloads the collision if the editor is modified, sets session.play to true.

returns.desc: False if no session exists, true otherwise.

disableSimulation.desc: Stops the simulation: disables the AI of unlocked vehicles and the signals, sets session.play to false.

returns.desc: False if no session exists, true otherwise.

getSessionData.desc: Returns the current session table (vehicles, lights, signs, name, author, play...), not copied.

returns.desc: Session, nil until it is created.

loadSession.desc: Loads a session from a JSON file: resets the session, restores options and metadata, loads the associated prefab if it exists then recreates vehicles and signals. Without an argument, resumes the remembered file after a level confirmation request (and disables assertLevel). Failure notification if the file is unreadable.

saveSession.desc: Saves the session to a JSON file and a prefab of the same name. No effect without a path.

onEditorInitialized.desc: Editor initialization hook: creates the trafficEditMode edit mode (shortcuts click, Shift+click move, Alt) and registers the windows.

onWindowMenuItem.desc: Menu hook: creates the session and checks the SimGroup if needed, clears the selection and shows the main window.

onEditorGui.desc: Editor frame hook: draws the Traffic Manager windows (only when the current edit mode is Traffic Manager) and the debug.

onUpdate.desc: Update hook: if the SimGroup has disappeared, resets the session; otherwise stores the vehicles that appeared in the SimGroup, updates the statistics and a 0.25 s timer.

onVehicleSpawned.desc: Hook called when a vehicle spawns: if the vehicles or signs window is active, creates the SimGroup if needed and queues the vehicle to be added to the session on the next frame.

onVehicleResetted.desc: Hook called when a vehicle is reset: recreates its session data (statistics reset to zero).

onSerialize.desc: Hook before Lua reload; returns an empty table.

onDeserialized.desc: Hook after Lua reload; does nothing.
